title: Pre-Analysis — Extension of the Fwd Lower Shell Bonded Doubler Strap to the Later MSN Band
abstract: Pre-analysis of extending the bonded doubler strap standard to aircraft beyond the original MSN band, run alongside the operator order that also produced the machined splice candidate.

sections.objective: Decide whether the bonded doubler strap released against the lower shell lap joint should be extended to the later MSN band, where the same operator has begun to report the same fastener hole findings. The order that raised the question also produced a candidate to replace the joint outright, so the analysis had to say not only whether the strap works on the later build but whether extending it is worth doing when a replacement is in pre-analysis behind it.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and two conditions came out of them. The strap standard supersedes the original interfay sealing answer, and on the later build a proportion of aircraft are still at that first standard, so extending the strap means completing a supersession that was left half done rather than starting a clean population. The oldest re-sealing bulletin remains effective on exactly those aircraft and its wording does not anticipate a third generation of answer. A published flush bonded skin repair on the same panel was found only by the descriptive text, sharing no identifier with the strap at all, and an aircraft carrying it cannot take the strap without a repair assessment. The chromate-free protection standard applies to the strap faying surface and its availability at the target stations sets the earliest date the extension can run.
sections.next_steps: Extend the strap effectivity to the later MSN band on condition that the first-generation aircraft in that band are brought to the strap standard in the same visit, and state that explicitly rather than leaving it to the operator to work out. Re-state the re-sealing bulletin effectivity. Add a pre-embodiment repair survey step so that a patched panel is assessed before the strap is quoted. Take the station readiness date from the surface protection analysis rather than assuming it.

similarity_seeds: external bonded strap over a longitudinal lap joint
flush bonded repair patch on a thinned lower shell skin
interfay sealing renewal on a forward fuselage joint

tasks.title: Establish the joint standard distribution across the later MSN band
Review published repairs on the same skin panel
Confirm surface protection availability at the target stations

expected_findings.rationale: A proportion of the later MSN band is still at the first-generation interfay sealing standard. Extending the strap into that band completes a supersession rather than starting a clean population, and the two cannot be left coexisting on the same joint.
expected_findings.resolution: State in the extended effectivity that first-generation aircraft are brought to the strap standard in the same visit.

expected_findings.rationale: The re-sealing bulletin is effective on aircraft not yet at the strap standard. Widening the strap changes which aircraft that describes, and the bulletin's own wording gives an operator no way to tell.
expected_findings.resolution: Re-state the bulletin effectivity in terms of the strap standard rather than in terms of the MSN band.

evidence.similarity_note: The repair and the strap describe work on the same material in entirely unrelated vocabulary — 'flush bonded patch for a thinned or cracked lower forward barrel skin' against 'external bonded doubler strap over the lap joint' — and share no part number, no drawing, no functional item number and no zone. Only the descriptive text links them.

expected_findings.rationale: An aircraft carrying the flush patch has a machined recess and a bond line in the area the strap covers. The combined configuration is not substantiated and the patch bond line cannot be inspected once the strap is bonded over it.
expected_findings.resolution: Add a pre-embodiment repair survey to the retrofit bulletin so a patched panel is assessed before the strap is quoted.

expected_findings.rationale: The strap faying surface is protected with the replacement conversion system. Its availability at the stations that would run the extension sets the earliest date the extension can start.
expected_findings.resolution: Take the station readiness date from the surface protection analysis instead of assuming it.

expected_non_findings.reason: Describes an external doubler repair at a longitudinal seam in almost the same words as the strap itself and sits in the same two-digit chapter, but it applies to the aft fuselage skin. It shares no part number, no drawing and no zone with the forward lower shell and cannot be affected by work in section 13.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a positive position subject to two conditions: first-generation aircraft in the band are brought to the strap standard in the same visit, and a repair survey precedes the quotation on any patched panel.
